title: Post-traumatic distress syndrome in childhood cancer patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation
summary: The aim of this study is to find out how often children develop post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) after a stem cell transplant or specific cell therapy and which factors increase the risk of this. We want to investigate the extent to which certain personality traits, the children's confidence in their own ability to deal with problems, their quality of life and current stress levels influence the risk of PTSD. For this purpose, standardized questionnaires will be used as well as biological measurements in the blood in order to record the stress level in the body and compare it with the questionnaire results. The results of the study should help to develop better psychological support services for children with cancer so that they can better cope with their trauma. The long-term goal is to reduce the risk of PTSD and improve the quality of life of children with cancer.

interventions.name: In a prospective study of 50 children, aged between 5 - 22 years, receiving hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) and/or specific cell therapy, the occurrence of PTSD will be investigated.
